stops.title: Solubility, Henry's law & Raoult's law
stops.inShort: Henry's law: solubility S = K_H P (at constant T). Raoult's law for volatile liquids: P_total = P₁° x₁ + P₂° x₂. Ideal solutions obey Raoult's law with ΔH_mix = 0, ΔV_mix = 0.

stops.title: Lowering of vapour pressure & Boiling point elevation
stops.inShort: Relative lowering of vapour pressure: (P₁° − P₁)/P₁° = x₂ ≈ (W₂ M₁)/(M₂ W₁). Boiling point elevation: ΔT_b = K_b m, so M₂ = (1000 K_b W₂)/(ΔT_b W₁).

stops.title: Freezing point depression & Osmotic pressure
stops.inShort: Freezing point depression: ΔT_f = K_f m. Osmotic pressure: π = M R T = (W₂ R T)/(M₂ V). Reverse osmosis occurs when applied pressure exceeds osmotic pressure (P > π).

stops.title: Colligative properties of electrolytes & van't Hoff factor
stops.inShort: van't Hoff factor i = (normal molar mass)/(observed molar mass) = (observed colligative property)/(calculated property). Degree of dissociation α = (i − 1)/(n − 1). Modified formulas: ΔT_f = i K_f m, π = i M R T.

items.f: ΔT_f = i K_f m,  π = i C R T = i (n₂/V) R T
items.s: i = 1 for non-electrolytes like urea, glucose, sucrose.

board.text: The freezing point of 0.1 m aqueous solution of urea, if K_f for water is 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹ is ____.
What is the molality of an aqueous solution of KBr having freezing point −3.72°C (K_f for water is 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹)?

points.text: ΔT_f = i K_f m with i = 2 giving m = 1 mol/kg

board.text: (a) State Henry's law. (b) Define: Osmotic pressure.
board.answer:
(a) Henry's law: The solubility of a gas in a liquid at constant temperature is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas above the solution (S = K_H P).
(b) Osmotic pressure: The excess hydrostatic pressure that must be applied on the solution side to just stop the spontaneous flow of solvent into the solution through a semipermeable membrane.

board.text: Write the condition of reverse osmosis.
board.answer: Applied external pressure on the solution side must be greater than the osmotic pressure of the solution (P_applied > π).

board.text: Henry's constant for CH₃Br(g) is 0.159 mol dm⁻³ bar⁻¹ at 25°C. Calculate its solubility in water at 25°C, if its partial pressure is 0.164 bar.
What is osmotic pressure? How will you determine molar mass of solute from osmotic pressure?
board.answer:
Osmotic pressure (π) is the excess pressure applied to the solution to stop osmosis.
For dilute solutions, π = C R T = (n₂ / V) R T.
Substituting n₂ = W₂ / M₂:
π = (W₂ R T) / (M₂ V) ⇒ M₂ = (W₂ R T) / (π V).
